stepExplanation: In bipedal hominins, the foramen magnum (hole where the spinal cord exits the skull) is positioned underneath the skull rather than at the back. This allows the head to balance directly on top of the vertebral column, essential for upright posture. In quadrupedal apes, the foramen magnum is positioned more posteriorly.
